doc.title: Von Freeman — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Choral playing and hymn harmony with Dyett
summary: He praises Dyett's training in four-part hymns and spirituals as the best lesson in harmony.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Learning your horn: teachers, lessons and fees

blocks.x: I know, but you’re talking about as a saxophone player or singing?
Just music in general. It’s good for piano players and everybody. It’s three- and four-note harmony – two-, three-, four-note harmony.
But you’re not talking about Bach or something like that.
No, this is just – Captain Walter Dyett had what he called . . .
Yeah, and all those different – like if you listen to a great singing group, this is what they’re really doing.
I know what you’re talking about, with the moving parts and things like that.
Four parts, yeah. Man, this opens you up entirely, because you get a chance to hear all the variations of chords.
